rows.question: For the RBAC action 'access_as_shared' (considering only IPv4 subnets), what are the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of subnet IP version with subtotals and a grand total, and—alongside those stats—what are the top 3 shared networks by subnet count, including each network ID, its subnet count, and the tenant ID of each subnet (with repeated network IDs suppressed)? Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH SubnetStats AS (
  SELECT
    network_id,
    ip_version,
    COUNT(*) AS subnet_count,
    tenant_id
  FROM ipallocations
  WHERE ip_address LIKE '%[0-9]%'
  GROUP BY network_id, ip_version
),
TopNetworks AS (
  SELECT
    network_id,
    subnet_count
  FROM SubnetStats
  ORDER BY subnet_count DESC
  LIMIT 3
)
SELECT
  AVG(subnet_count) AS average_subnet_count,
  STDDEV(subnet_count) AS variance_subnet_count,
  STDDEV(subnet_count) AS standard_deviation_subnet_count,
  (
    SELECT
      network_id,
      subnet_count
    FROM TopNetworks
  ) AS top_3_networks,
  (
    SELECT
      tenant_id
    FROM ipallocations
    WHERE ip_address LIKE '%[0-9]%'
      AND network_id IN (SELECT network_id FROM TopNetworks)
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  ) AS all_tenant_ids
FROM SubnetStats

rows.question: For tenants that are in the top 10 by distinct DOWN ports and also in the top 10 by IPv4 subnet count, return the tenant ID, total distinct DOWN ports, whether any of those DOWN ports have an IP allocation, total IPv4 subnets, and whether any IPv4 subnet has a standard attribute record with a non-null updated-at timestamp—keeping only tenants where DOWN ports are more than 75% of their IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  t.id AS tenant_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.port_id) AS total_distinct_down_ports,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(ia.ip_address) > 0 THEN 'Yes'
    ELSE 'No'
  END AS has_down_ports_with_ip_allocation,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS total_ipv4_subnets,
  CASE
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT
        1
      FROM
        ipamsubnets
      JOIN
        ipallocations ON ipamsubnets.id = ipallocations.ipam_subnet_id
      WHERE
        ipallocations.ip_address IS NOT NULL
    ) THEN 'Yes'
    ELSE 'No'
  END AS has_ipv4_subnets_with_updated_at
FROM tenants AS t
JOIN ports AS p
  ON t.id = p.tenant_id
JOIN ipallocations AS ia
  ON p.port_id = ia.port_id
JOIN ipamsubnets AS us
  ON ia.ipam_subnet_id = us.id
GROUP BY
  t.id
HAVING
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.port_id) > 7 AND COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) > 7

rows.question: How many distinct admin_state_up = 1 ports that are bound to a security group are there, and how many distinct DOWN ports belong to security groups whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per security group? Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH focused_whole_view AS (
SELECT
  COUNT(p.id)
FROM ports AS p
WHERE
  p.admin_state_up = 1
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS distinct_up_ports,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 0 THEN p.id ELSE NULL END) AS distinct_down_ports
FROM ports AS p
WHERE
  p.admin_state_up = 1
GROUP BY
  p.tenant_id
HAVING
  COUNT(
    CASE
      WHEN p.admin_state_up = 0
      THEN p.id
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) > (
    SELECT
      AVG(down_count)
    FROM (
      SELECT
        COUNT(
        CASE
          WHEN p2.admin_state_up = 0
          THEN p2.id
          ELSE NULL
        END
      ) AS down_count
      FROM ports AS p2
      INNER JOIN securitygroups AS sg ON p2.tenant_id = sg.tenant_id
    ) AS down_counts
  )

rows.question: For external networks that are marked as default (IS_DEFAULT = 0), list each network’s ID, name, status, and ADMIN_STATE_UP, along with (1) the per-status average ADMIN_STATE_UP computed as a window over networks ordered by name, (2) the overall average of those per-status averages across all statuses, and (3) the overall benchmark ADMIN_STATE_UP across all such external networks and a category showing whether each network is ABOVE_BENCHMARK, BELOW_BENCHMARK, or AT_BENCHMARK versus that benchmark. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH ExternalNetworks AS (
    SELECT
        network_id
    FROM
        externalnetworks
    WHERE
        is_default = 0
),
NetworkStats AS (
    SELECT
        n.id AS network_id,
        n.name AS network_name,
        n.status AS network_status,
        n.admin_state_up AS network_admin_state_up
    FROM
        networks n
    JOIN
        ExternalNetworks en ON n.id = en.network_id
),
PerStatusAverages AS (
    SELECT
        network_id,
        AVG(network_admin_state_up) AS avg_admin_state_up
    FROM
        NetworkStats
    GROUP BY
        network_id
)
SELECT
    en.network_id,
    n.name AS network_name,
    n.status AS network_status,
    n.admin_state_up,
    (
        SELECT
            AVG(avg_admin_state_up)
        FROM
            PerStatusAverages
    ) AS overall_avg_admin_state_up,
    CASE
        WHEN n.admin_state_up = (
            SELECT
                AVG(avg_admin_state_up)
            FROM
                PerStatusAverages
        ) THEN 'AT_BENCHMARK'
        WHEN n.admin_state_up > (
            SELECT
                AVG(avg_admin_state_up)
            FROM
                PerStatusAverages
        ) THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK'
        ELSE 'BELOW_BENCHMARK'
    END AS benchmark_category
FROM
    externalnetworks en
JOIN
    networks n ON en.network_id = n.id
WHERE
    en.is_default = 0
ORDER BY
    n.name

rows.question: For IPv4 subnets that are in the top 10 by DNS nameserver order range and that have DNS nameservers configured, return the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first and last IP (only where the first IP is the minimum for that subnet), the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows by subnet ID, plus the DNS nameserver order range and order variance. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH RankedSubnets AS (
    SELECT
        s.id AS subnet_id,
        s.name AS subnet_name,
        s.tenant_id,
        s.network_id,
        s.ip_version,
        s.cidr,
        s.gateway_ip,
        s.enable_dhcp,
        sp.first_ip,
        sp.last_ip,
        std.standard_attr_id,
        std.standard_attr_id,
        std.standard_attr_id,
        std.standard_attr_id,
        std.standard_attr_id,
        s.order AS dns_order
    FROM
        subnets s
    JOIN
        ipamallocationpools sp ON s.id = sp.subnet_id
    JOIN
        subnetpools sp2 ON s.id = sp2.id
    JOIN
        networks n ON s.network_id = n.id
    JOIN
        subnetpools std ON s.id = std.id
)
SELECT
    rs.subnet_name,
    rs.tenant_id,
    rs.network_id,
    rs.ip_version,
    rs.cidr,
    rs.gateway_ip,
    rs.enable_dhcp,
    rs.first_ip,
    rs.last_ip,
    (
        SELECT
            standard_attr_id
        FROM
            subnetpools
        WHERE
            subnet_id = rs.subnet_id
        ORDER BY
            standard_attr_id
        LIMIT 1
    ) AS max_standard_attr_id,
    (
        SELECT
            standard_attr_id
        FROM
            subnetpools
        WHERE
            subnet_id = rs.subnet_id
        ORDER BY
            standard_attr_id
        LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
    ) AS max_standard_attr_id_row2,
    (
        SELECT
            standard_attr_id
        FROM
            subnetpools
        WHERE
            subnet_id = rs.subnet_id
        ORDER BY
            standard_attr_id
        LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2
    ) AS max_standard_attr_id_row3,
    (
        SELECT
            dns_order
        FROM
            RankedSubnets
        WHERE
            subnet_id = rs.subnet_id
        ORDER BY
            dns_order
        LIMIT 1
    ) AS dns_order,
    (
        SELECT
            dns_order
        FROM
            RankedSubnets
        WHERE
            subnet_id = rs.subnet_id
        ORDER BY
            dns_order
        LIMIT 1
    ) AS dns_order_variance
FROM
    RankedSubnets rs
WHERE
    rs.ip_version = 4
ORDER BY
    rs.dns_order
LIMIT 10

rows.question: Show a combined report of DOWN ports that (1) lists ports by tenant with port ID, tenant ID (not repeated on consecutive rows), binding host, VIF type, allocated IP address, a row number ordered by IP address using a 2-preceding/1-following window, plus a subtotal row per tenant with the total number of DOWN ports; and (2) lists ports by VIF type with port name, MAC address, admin_state_up, binding host, the windowed average admin_state_up over 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address, plus a subtotal row per VIF type with the total number of DOWN ports and the average of the windowed values, with VIF type not repeated on consecutive rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH ports_down AS (
  SELECT
    p.port_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.device_id AS binding_host,
    CASE
      WHEN p.mac_address IS NOT NULL THEN 'VIF'
      ELSE 'Port'
    END AS vif_type,
    CASE
      WHEN p.mac_address IS NOT NULL THEN p.mac_address
      ELSE NULL
    END AS ip_address,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ip_address) AS port_rank,
    COUNT(port_id) OVER (PARTITION BY p.tenant_id) AS total_down_ports,
    COUNT(port_id) OVER (PARTITION BY p.vif_type) AS total_down_ports_by_vif_type,
    AVG(admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY p.vif_type) AS avg_admin_state_up_by_vif_type
  FROM ports
  WHERE admin_state_up = 1
)
SELECT
  port_id,
  tenant_id,
  binding_host,
  vif_type,
  ip_address,
  port_rank,
  total_down_ports,
  total_down_ports_by_vif_type,
  avg_admin_state_up_by_vif_type
FROM ports_down
ORDER BY port_rank

rows.question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with its RBAC action and target tenant (including the distinct RBAC target-tenant count per network and the dense-rank window column), and also include—alongside every such network/RBAC row—the per-(port status, device owner) port counts for ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp for each group, and each group’s deviation from the overall average port count. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH networks_active AS (
  SELECT
    id AS network_id,
    name AS network_name,
    status,
    admin_state_up
  FROM networks
  WHERE
    status != 'deleted' AND admin_state_up = 1
),
ports_active AS (
  SELECT
    p.port_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.name AS port_name,
    p.network_id,
    p.mac_address,
    p.admin_state_up AS port_admin_state_up,
    p.status AS port_status,
    p.device_id,
    p.device_owner,
    p.dns_name,
    p.standard_attr_id,
    DATE_FORMAT(p.standard_attr_updated, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') AS standard_attr_updated
  FROM ports p
  WHERE
    p.admin_state_up = 1
),
port_counts AS (
  SELECT
    port_id,
    COUNT(*) AS port_count
  FROM ports_active
  GROUP BY port_id
),
port_status_counts AS (
  SELECT
    port_status,
    COUNT(*) AS port_count
  FROM ports_active
  GROUP BY port_status
),
ranked_ports AS (
  SELECT
    p.port_id,
    p.port_name,
    p.port_status,
    p.device_owner,
    pc.port_count,
    psc.port_count AS down_port_count,
    DATE_FORMAT(p.standard_attr_updated, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') AS standard_attr_updated,
    STDDEV(pc.port_count) AS port_count_variance
  FROM ports_active p
  JOIN port_counts pc ON p.port_id = pc.port_id
  JOIN port_status_counts psc ON p.port_status = psc.port_count
  GROUP BY p.port_id, p.port_name, p.port_status, p.device_owner, p.standard_attr_updated
)
SELECT
  n.network_name AS 'Network Name',
  n.status AS 'Network Status',
  n.admin_state_up AS 'Network Admin State Up',
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.port_id) AS 'Distinct Port Count',
  SUM(CASE WHEN r.down_port_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS 'Down Port Count',
  AVG(CASE WHEN r.down_port_count > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS 'Average Down Port Ratio',
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.port_id) AS 'Distinct Port Count',
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.port_id) AS 'Distinct Port Count'
FROM networks_active n
JOIN ranked_ports r ON n.network_name = r.port_name
GROUP BY n.network_name, n.status, n.admin_state_up
ORDER BY
  n.network_name

rows.question: For ports whose status is DOWN and that also have a standard attribute ID above the average for their resource type, list each port’s port ID and tenant ID along with host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the IP-address-ordered row number (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the overall average DOWN-port count benchmark and the tenant usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER), plus the port’s MAC address and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within its resource type. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH PortStats AS (
    SELECT
        p.id AS port_id,
        p.tenant_id,
        p.name,
        p.mac_address,
        p.admin_state_up,
        p.ip_address,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY p.ip_address) AS ip_address_order,
        p.tenant_id,
        p.tenant_id
    FROM ports AS p
    WHERE
        p.status = 'DOWN'
)
SELECT
    ps.port_id,
    ps.tenant_id,
    ps.name,
    ps.mac_address,
    ps.admin_state_up,
    ps.ip_address,
    ps.ip_address_order,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ports WHERE tenant_id = ps.tenant_id AND status = 'DOWN') AS total_down_ports,
    (SELECT AVG(count(*)) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM ports WHERE tenant_id = ps.tenant_id AND status = 'DOWN') AS down_counts) AS avg_down_ports,
    CASE
        WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ports WHERE tenant_id = ps.tenant_id AND status = 'DOWN') * 1.5 > (SELECT AVG(count(*)) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM ports WHERE tenant_id = ps.tenant_id AND status = 'DOWN') AS down_counts) * 1.5
        THEN 'HIGH_USER'
        WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ports WHERE tenant_id = ps.tenant_id AND status = 'DOWN') * 1.5 < (SELECT AVG(count(*)) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM ports WHERE tenant_id = ps.tenant_id AND status = 'DOWN') AS down_counts) * 1.5
        THEN 'LOW_USER'
        ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER'
    END AS tenant_usage_category,
    (SELECT SUM(standardattributes.id) FROM standardattributes WHERE standardattributes.resource_type = p.standard_attr_id) AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids
FROM PortStats AS ps

rows.question: How many DOWN ports have IP allocations (from the DOWN-port per-network allocation analysis) and how many administratively up ports have port security bindings (from the admin-up port security benchmark analysis)? Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each port as 'HIGH_SECURITY' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_SECURITY' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_SECURITY'.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH focused_whole_view AS (
SELECT
  COUNT(p.id)
FROM ports AS p
WHERE
  p.admin_state_up = 1
)
SELECT
    COUNT(CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN p.id END) AS down_port_count,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM portbindingports WHERE port_id = p.id) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM portsecuritybindings WHERE port_id = p.id AND port_security_enabled = 1) THEN p.id END) AS high_security_port_count
FROM ports p
LEFT JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id
LEFT JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id

rows.question: For ports whose status is DOWN, show each port’s ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include, per host, the total number of DOWN-port IP allocations and each row’s deviation from the average DOWN-port IP allocations per host, and attach the DOWN-status port-security-binding rollup statistics (admin-state label plus the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of port security bindings per port, including subtotal/grand-total style labels). Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  p.port_id,
  p.tenant_id,
  p.host,
  ia.ip_address AS vif_ip_address,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ia.ip_address ORDER BY ia.ip_address ASC ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS row_num,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ia.ip_address) OVER (PARTITION BY p.host) AS total_down_ip_allocations,
  (COUNT(DISTINCT ia.ip_address) OVER (PARTITION BY p.host) - (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ia2.ip_address) FROM ipallocations ia2 WHERE ia2.port_id = p.port_id)) AS ip_allocation_deviation,
  (
    SELECT
      SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'DOWN' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    FROM ports p
    WHERE p.port_id = p.port_id
  ) AS port_security_rollup
FROM ipallocations ia
JOIN ports p ON ia.port_id = p.port_id
WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'
ORDER BY ia.ip_address

rows.question: For each of the top 10 tenants with the highest total number of IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), list the tenant ID, the total number of such ports, the total number of IP allocations across those ports, whether the tenant has any floating IPs allocated, and the average (across that tenant’s ports) deviation of each port’s IP allocation count from the global average IP allocation count across all such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH port_ip_counts AS (
    SELECT
        p.tenant_id,
        COUNT(i.ip_address) AS num_ip_allocations
    FROM
        ipallocations i
    JOIN
        ports p ON i.port_id = p.id
    WHERE
        p.admin_state_up = 1
    GROUP BY
        p.tenant_id
),
tenant_summary AS (
    SELECT
        t.tenant_id,
        SUM(t.num_ip_allocations) AS total_ip_allocations,
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM port_ip_counts pc WHERE pc.tenant_id = t.tenant_id) AS num_ports_with_allocations
    FROM
        port_ip_counts t
    GROUP BY
        t.tenant_id
)
SELECT
    ts.tenant_id,
    ts.total_ip_allocations,
    ts.num_ports_with_allocations,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ipallocations i WHERE i.port_id IN (SELECT id FROM ports WHERE admin_state_up = 1)) AS has_floating_ips,
    AVG(ts.total_ip_allocations - (SELECT AVG(total_ip_allocations) FROM tenant_summary)) AS avg_ip_allocation_deviation
FROM
    tenant_summary ts
JOIN
    (SELECT tenant_id FROM port_ip_counts) t ON ts.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
WHERE t.tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM port_ip_counts)
GROUP BY
    ts.tenant_id
ORDER BY
    ts.total_ip_allocations DESC
LIMIT 10

tenant_down_counts(tenant_id, tenant_down_count) AS tenant_down_counts,

rows.question: For the top 10 tenants with the highest total number of IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), and where more than 75% of the tenant’s ports are in DOWN status, return the tenant ID, total number of such administratively up ports, total IP allocations across them, whether the tenant has any floating IPs, plus the number of DOWN ports whose standard attribute ID is above the DOWN-port average for their resource type and the average running sum of standard attribute IDs for those qualifying DOWN ports. rows.question: For ports bound to security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID of other ports in the same network, show each port’s ID, status, allocated IP address, and the running sum of its standard attribute ID within its network; also include (for the matching port status) the port-security rollup label (Enabled/Disabled, including subtotals and grand total rows) and the corresponding count of ports. Do not return any rounded answers.

SELECT
  p.id AS ports_id,
  p.status AS ports_status,
  ia.ip_address,
  SUM(p.standard_attr_id) OVER (PARTITION BY p.network_id) AS running_sum_std_attr_id,
  CASE
    WHEN n.id IN (
      SELECT
        network_id
      FROM networksecuritybindings
      WHERE

  END AS port_security_rollup_label,
  COUNT(p.id) AS port_count
FROM ports AS p
JOIN ipallocations AS ia
  ON p.id = ia.port_id
JOIN networks AS n
  ON p.network_id = n.id
JOIN networksecuritybindings AS nsb
  ON n.id = nsb.network_id
WHERE
  nsb.port_security_enabled = 1
  AND p.network_id IN (
    SELECT
      network_id
    FROM networksecuritybindings
    WHERE
      port_security_enabled = 1
  )
  AND p.standard_attr_id > (
    SELECT
      AVG(standard_attr_id)
    FROM ports AS port_avg
    WHERE
      port_avg.network_id = p.network_id
  )
GROUP BY
  p.id,
  p.status

rows.question: For ports whose status is DOWN, restricted to tenants that are in the top 10 by total IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include, for each tenant, the total number of DOWN ports and the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, along with that tenant’s total number of administratively up ports, total IP allocations on those ports, and whether the tenant has any floating IPs allocated. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH TenantRank AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'DOWN' THEN 1 END) AS down_port_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN admin_state_up = 1 THEN 1 END) AS total_up_ports,
        SUM(ip_allocations.ip_address) AS total_ip_allocations
    FROM ports
    JOIN ipallocations ON ports.id = ipallocations.port_id
    WHERE ports.admin_state_up = 1
    GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
    pi.port_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.mac_address AS host,
    v.vlan AS vif_type,
    ip.ip_address,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.tenant_id ORDER BY ip.ip_address ASC ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS row_num
FROM ports AS p
JOIN ipallocations AS ip ON p.id = ipallocations.port_id
JOIN networks AS n ON p.network_id = n.id
JOIN vips AS v ON p.port_id = v.port_id
WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'
AND p.admin_state_up = 1
AND p.tenant_id IN (
    SELECT
        tenant_id
    FROM ports
    WHERE
        admin_state_up = 1
    GROUP BY
        tenant_id
    ORDER BY
        down_port_count DESC
    LIMIT 10

ORDER BY

    row_num

rows.question: For IPv4 subnets whose DNS nameserver order range is greater than the average order range across all IPv4 subnets, list each subnet name along with its DNS nameserver order range, order variance, coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the order values, and the deviation of that coefficient from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH focused_whole_view AS (
SELECT
  COUNT(p.id)
FROM ports AS p
WHERE
  p.admin_state_up = 1
)
SELECT
  s.name AS subnet_name,
  ds.order AS dns_nameserver_order,
  variance(ds.order) AS order_variance,
  STDDEV(ds.order) AS coefficient_of_variation,
  STDDEV(ds.order) AS deviation_from_average_coefficient_of_variation
FROM subnets s
JOIN dnsnameservers ds
  ON s.id = ds.subnet_id
WHERE
  s.ip_version = 4
GROUP BY
  s.id,
  s.name
ORDER BY
  order_variance

rows.question: For the top 10 tenants ranked by the highest coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) divided by average) of allocated IP address string lengths for ports with port security enabled, list each tenant’s ID, their coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), and whether they have any ACTIVE, DOWN, or BUILD ports; and for those same tenants, show details of their DOWN ports including port ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port count across tenants as a benchmark, and the tenant’s DOWN-port usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER). Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  t.id AS tenant_id,
  (
    STDDEV(LENGTH(ip_allocations.ip_address))
    / AVG(LENGTH(ip_allocations.ip_address))
  ) AS coefficient_of_variation,
  GROUP_CONCAT(
    CASE
      WHEN p.admin_state_up = 0
      THEN
        CASE
          WHEN p.status = 'down' THEN 'DOWN'
          WHEN p.status = 'active' THEN 'ACTIVE'
          WHEN p.status = 'warm' THEN 'BUILD'
          ELSE 'UNKNOWN'
        END
      ELSE
        'UNKNOWN'
    END
  ) AS port_statuses,
  (
    SELECT
      GROUP_CONCAT(
        CASE
          WHEN p2.admin_state_up = 0
          THEN
            p2.port_id
          ELSE
            NULL
        END
      )
    FROM ports p2
    WHERE p2.tenant_id = t.id AND p2.admin_state_up = 0
  ) AS down_port_ids
FROM
  ipallocations
JOIN
  ports p ON ipallocations.port_id = p.id
JOIN
  members m ON ipallocations.port_id = m.port_id
JOIN
  tenants t ON m.tenant_id = t.id
GROUP BY
  t.id
ORDER BY
  coefficient_of_variation DESC
LIMIT 10

rows.question: For subnets on networks that have a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', show each subnet name and gateway IP (including subtotals per subnet name and a grand total) along with the maximum IP version (keeping only rows where this maximum is greater than 3). Also, for any matching IPv4 subnet name, include its dense rank of the associated standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp (using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows), the overall average of these dense ranks as a benchmark, and the subnet’s rank category (HIGH_RANK/LOW_RANK/AVERAGE_RANK). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each subnet as 'HIGH_RANK' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_RANK' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_RANK'.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  s.name AS subnet_name,
  s.gateway_ip,
  SUM(s.ip_version) AS subnet_total_ip_version,
  MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version
FROM subnets s
JOIN networks n
  ON s.tenant_id = n.tenant_id
WHERE
  n.status = 'access_as_shared'
GROUP BY
  s.name,
  s.gateway_ip
HAVING
  MAX(s.ip_version) > 3
ORDER BY
  MAX(s.ip_version) DESC

rows.question: For IPv4 subnets whose network RBAC action is set to 'access_as_shared', what are the subnet name, CIDR, RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IP version (ordered by standard attribute ID), the total number of such shared subnets per target tenant and the average of those totals across all target tenants, along with the subnet’s standard attribute resource type and the dense rank of its standard attribute (ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows)? Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH shared_ipv4_subnets AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.name AS subnet_name,
    s.cidr AS subnet_cidr,
    s.tenant_id AS subnet_tenant_id,
    s.standard_attr_id
  FROM subnet AS s
  WHERE
    s.ip_version = 4
    AND s.admin_state_up = 1
    AND s.rbac_action = 'access_as_shared'
),
running_sums AS (
  SELECT
    subnet_name,
    subnet_tenant_id,
    SUM(standard_attr_id) OVER (PARTITION BY subnet_tenant_id ORDER BY standard_attr_id) AS running_sum_standard_attr_id
  FROM shared_ipv4_subnets
),
tenant_counts AS (
  SELECT
    subnet_tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_shared_subnets_per_tenant
  FROM shared_ipv4_subnets
  GROUP BY subnet_tenant_id
)
SELECT
  rs.subnet_name,
  rs.subnet_cidr,
  rs.subnet_tenant_id,
  rs.running_sum_standard_attr_id,
  tc.total_shared_subnets_per_tenant,
  AVG(tc.total_shared_subnets_per_tenant) OVER () AS average_total_subnet_counts,
  rs.standard_attr_id,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY rs.standard_attr_id ASC, rs.standard_attr_id ASC) AS dense_rank_standard_attr_id
FROM running_sums AS rs
JOIN tenant_counts AS tc
  ON rs.subnet_tenant_id = tc.subnet_tenant_id
GROUP BY rs.subnet_name, rs.subnet_cidr, rs.subnet_tenant_id, rs.running_sum_standard_attr_id, rs.standard_attr_id, tc.total_shared_subnets_per_tenant
